Pre-K-K.vocabulary_notes: Use familiar concrete words, gentle repetition, simple action verbs, and at most one clearly explained new word.
Pre-K-K.sentence_complexity_notes: Use one or two short sentences per page, mostly subject-verb-object patterns, with a predictable refrain where natural.
Pre-K-K.illustration_style: Original preschool editorial illustration: large simple friendly forms, clean bold outlines, coral, sunflower and teal accents, cheerful flat color, minimal background clutter. No glossy 3D rendering. Meaningful objects fill the composition.
Pre-K-K.skill_notes: Emergent learners: adult-read directions, familiar words, count within 10, simple shape/word matching, first-letter recognition, large drawing and tracing spaces. No independent reading passages.

1st-2nd.vocabulary_notes: Use decodable high-frequency language plus a few context-supported descriptive words; make meaning inferable from the scene.
1st-2nd.sentence_complexity_notes: Use mostly simple sentences with occasional conjunctions, varied openings, dialogue tags, and a clear chronological sequence.
1st-2nd.illustration_style: Premium early-elementary activity-book art: expressive hand-drawn shapes, crisp outlines, warm vibrant flat colors and restrained paper texture, clear large subjects and purposeful scenes. No glossy 3D mascot thumbnails or busy backgrounds.
1st-2nd.skill_notes: Foundational literacy, short concrete passages, addition/subtraction within 100, classification, sentence writing. Avoid content requiring advanced decoding.

3rd-4th.vocabulary_notes: Use vivid grade-appropriate vocabulary, meaningful context clues, sensory detail, and domain words when the lesson calls for them.
3rd-4th.sentence_complexity_notes: Mix simple, compound, and accessible complex sentences; use dialogue and interior thought while keeping paragraphs compact.
3rd-4th.illustration_style: Polished illustrated learning journal: clear purposeful diagrams and visual narratives, bold controlled color, detailed but readable scenes, energetic editorial composition. Age-respectful, no babyish mascot repetition.
3rd-4th.skill_notes: Multi-step thinking, multiplication facts and exact division, evidence from short informational passages, word relationships, explain choices. Do not use babyish counting tasks.
3rd-4th.reading_guidance: Write for ages 8-10: concrete explanations and relatable examples, mostly short sentences, clear transitions, and a few essential terms defined naturally. Require text-supported inference without adult academic jargon.

5th-6th.vocabulary_notes: Use precise, nuanced vocabulary, figurative language in moderation, subject-specific terms with natural context, and no condescending baby talk.
5th-6th.sentence_complexity_notes: Use varied sentence lengths, controlled complex syntax, subtext in dialogue, stronger transitions, and age-appropriate reflection.
5th-6th.illustration_style: Sophisticated upper-elementary editorial illustration: precise contours, restrained rich palette, useful contextual scenes, clean information hierarchy and mature proportions. No babyish clip art.
5th-6th.skill_notes: Upper-elementary reasoning: authentic planning constraints, multi-digit arithmetic, precise vocabulary, inference and evidence, compare solutions, justify design decisions. No infantile clip art or tracing.
5th-6th.reading_guidance: Write for ages 10-12: explain meaningful real-world ideas with concrete examples, varied readable sentences, and essential vocabulary defined in context. Challenge reasoning through inference, comparison and text structure rather than dense academic language.
